name: Two-lane dated timeline
reader_question: In what order did two jurisdictions announce, enact and implement their measures?
relationship: Dated events from two parallel tracks placed on one date axis; marker style separates announcement, effective and implementation dates.
use_when: Two jurisdictions' measures need to be read against the same calendar
The gap between announcement, effective and implementation dates matters
avoid_when: More than two tracks must be compared — use swimlane
Events carry different evidence states rather than date types — use evidence-milestone-strip

data_contract.notes: Exactly two lanes; the first draws above the axis, the second below
Events within a lane in ascending order

units: Calendar dates on a linear day-count scale spanning whole calendar years.

editable: Markers, stems, axis band and labels as native shapes and text boxes
not_data_bound: Dates are positioned from the fixture at build time; moving an event requires dragging its marker, stem and label together

table_alternative: A dated event table with lane, measure, date type and date.
variations: Lanes split by instrument instead of jurisdiction
Shaded interval between announcement and effective date
limitations: Shared dates do not imply causation or response between lanes
Label stagger is limited to three levels per lane; dense clusters need the swimlane or a table

excluded_alternatives.reason: Loses which jurisdiction issued each measure

excluded_alternatives.form: Line chart of cumulative measure counts
excluded_alternatives.reason: Counts erase the differences between announcement, effective and implementation dates
